title: Marisol Cove homepage campaign: license three differently-lit coastal stock sources, match-grade them to one house warm-coastal look, cut six section heroes, triage the two brand marks, then data-merge a six-page section proof book
grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief for premium, luxury-style website hero banners with a 'clean, premium, modern design' and the 'ability to maintain consistent brand identity across all creative assets,' and laundered to a fictional boutique clifftop hotel, 'Marisol Cove' — no real hotel, brand, person, agency, marketplace, software or trademark is named anywhere. Only the sourcing site, Upwork, is named, as source.platform provenance (the hardness bar explicitly allows 'adapted from a real Upwork brief'); the stock library and the page-layout format are referred to generically. REPOSITIONED for connector reality and to remove the killed spec's fatal defects: the killed version (1) merged into a convert_pdf_to_indd output, whose fields do NOT bind; (2) tried to pull the desktop JPEG, the mobile PNG and the proof PDF as three SEPARATE per-artboard exports from document_render_layout, which can only export the WHOLE merged document; and (3) was a junior-hour single-hero grade. A skeptic then caught a fourth defect — UPSCALING: the proof book's @Hero frame is a full-bleed A4-landscape image at ~300 DPI (~3579 px across including 3 mm bleed), but the delivered heroes were web-sized (2400/1600 px), so binding a web crop full-bleed would have ENLARGED it. That is now fixed: each section gets a DISTINCT print-resolution hero crop (~3579 x 2551 px = 303 x 216 mm bleed edge at ~300 DPI, ~300 DPI effective at the 297 x 210 mm trim), a DOWNSCALE from the ~4500-5000 px stock source, bound to @Hero; the web-sized 2400/1600 px crops stay as separate website-hero deliverables — no upscaling anywhere in the merge. The original brief's out-of-scope 'AI image generation / realistic AI models' bonus is DELIBERATELY DROPPED (generative, banned). The corrected design is a real six-banner homepage CAMPAIGN: the hotel has no photography of its own, so the agent licenses THREE large widescreen coastal stock sources shot under DIFFERENT light, match-grades all three to ONE house warm-coastal look (the cross-asset failure gate), cuts SIX section heroes at BOTH print and web resolution from the three graded masters, triages the client's two brand marks (a flat wordmark that becomes clean vector line art vs a photographed embossed foil seal that must stay raster), and runs a genuinely hand-authored single-record layout template through a one-record-per-page data-merge into a single six-page press-ready proof book. NO generative expand / outpaint / upscale: every stock source is licensed large and cropped DOWN, never a small image stretched up.
one_line_ask: License three differently-lit widescreen coastal stock sources, decide per source how far to move white balance and exposure so all three land on one shared warm-coastal house look (a common warm-white on the whitewashed villa walls and one common soft-black in the cliff shadow), cut six section homepage heroes from the three graded masters at BOTH a print resolution that fills a full-bleed A4-landscape proof page at ~300 DPI as a downscale (never an enlargement) and a web resolution for the live site, prep the client's two brand marks each the correct way (the flat wordmark vectorized, the photographed embossed foil seal kept as a transparent raster, not traced), then data-merge the client's authored single-record layout template against the six-section roster to produce one press-ready six-page proof book, one section per page.
full_brief: Marisol Cove is a fictional boutique clifftop hotel on a sun-washed clifftop coast, rebuilding its homepage. The new homepage runs as six stacked full-width section bands — Stays, Weddings, Coastline, Spa, Dining and Contact — each with its own hero banner behind the headline, and the whole page has to read as ONE room: one light, one warmth, one premium mood, top to bottom. We do NOT have our own photography yet and we do NOT need the website built here — our developer handles the build. What we need is the hero imagery, finished and cohesive, plus a proof book we can sign off in the founders' meeting. Please source our heroes from a stock library: we want three high-resolution widescreen coastal shots — turquoise sea, whitewashed clifftop villas with terracotta roofs, white terrace parasols, generous open sky — each large enough that you can crop two different section banners out of it without ever enlarging it. Here is the catch, and it is the whole job: stock shots of the same coastline are taken at different times of day under different light, so out of the box they will NOT match — one will feel warm and amber, one cool and overcast, one shot straight into a golden sunset. If we drop three mismatched images down the page it looks cheap and broken. Your job is to bring all three to our single house 'warm-coastal' look — a soft, sun-warmed, premium feel where the whitewashed villa walls read as one consistent warm-white across all three images and the deep shade under the cliffs sits at one consistent soft near-black (deep, not crushed to dead black, never a clipped channel). Because the three start from different light, matching the OUTPUT means each needs a DIFFERENT correction: some want warming, some want cooling, some want an exposure lift and some a pull-down — pushing the same slider settings through all three will leave the page mismatched, and we will reject it. Be careful with the sunset frame in particular: judge it on its own walls, not on the instruction to 'make it golden' — if its walls already read as our warm-white, warming it further to chase the sunset will push it off the set. When you are done, hand us a short sheet listing, per source, the white-balance and exposure moves you dialed, so we can confirm the three were matched to one target and not just each 'auto-fixed' to look fine alone. From the three graded masters, cut our six section heroes: a wide cinematic band for the full-width sections (Stays, Coastline, Dining) and a taller framing for the feature sections (Weddings, Spa, Contact), each leaving clear open sky or open water on one side so our headline has room to breathe — do not let the buildings crowd the copy zone. One more thing about size, and it matters: those six section banners are web-sized, for our developer's live site. But the proof book we sign off prints FULL-BLEED at A4 landscape, so each section's hero also has to reach that page at true print resolution, filling the whole trim edge to edge at around 300 DPI. We refuse anything upscaled — so that print-sized hero has to be cut DOWN from the big stock source too, exactly like the web banners, never blown up from a web crop. So give us, per section, TWO cuts from the same graded master: a print-resolution hero that fills the full-bleed proof page as a genuine downscale, and a web-sized banner for the site. Next, our two brand marks, which are NOT the same kind of file and must not be treated the same: (1) our wordmark, a flat cream 'MARISOL COVE' lockup we are handing you as a slightly skewed scan on off-white paper — get it clean, straight and razor-sharp as crisp line art for every section masthead; (2) our founder's seal, the small embossed brass 'EST. MMXIX' medallion, which we are handing you as a close-up PHOTOGRAPH with all its metallic sheen and relief — it has to drop onto the pages with its shine intact and must NOT be turned into flat line art. Think about which mark can become vector and which one cannot survive it. Finally, assemble the proof: we have hand-built the section-proof layout template (a genuine authored .indd/.idml) with the real placeholder fields and three image slots (the section hero, the wordmark masthead, and the seal), and we are giving you the six-section roster with our headlines and sub-heads; merge them so every section gets its own proof page with its copy bound, its matching graded print-resolution hero placed full-bleed, the crisp wordmark in the masthead and the seal in the corner — then hand back one press-ready ~300 DPI A4-landscape PDF proof book covering all six sections, one section per page, for the sign-off deck. Bind our headlines and sub-heads verbatim from the roster; do not rewrite our copy. Acceptance: all three sources matched to one warm-coastal white point and one soft-black on their whitewashed-wall and cliff-shadow references; six section heroes cut from them with clean copy space and no upscaling anywhere — each section's full-bleed proof hero a genuine downscale from the large source landing at ~300 DPI at the page trim, distinct from the web-sized banner; the two marks prepped the correct way (one crisp vector, one transparent-ground raster with its sheen intact); and exactly one proof page per roster section.

inputs.name: marisol_section_proof_template.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built page-layout document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4-landscape (297 x 210 mm) homepage-section proof page with 3 mm bleed — ONE section per page. It must contain live data-merge placeholder fields <<section>>, <<headline>>, <<subhead>>, and THREE @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to three separate image frames: a FULL-BLEED section-hero frame (bleed edge 303 x 216 mm, i.e. ~3579 x 2551 px at ~300 DPI) bound to @Hero (the matching graded PRINT-resolution section crop, cut DOWN from the ~4500-5000 px stock source so filling the full-bleed frame is a DOWNSCALE at ~300 DPI effective at the 297 x 210 mm trim — never a web-sized crop enlarged to fill the page), a small cream masthead panel with a logo frame bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark), and a lower-corner frame bound to @Seal (the transparent-ground embossed foil seal). The masthead panel behind @Wordmark is a light CREAM band (so the vectorized wordmark's enclosed letter-counters, which trace filled-white on their off-white ground, read correctly on light — never a dark-ground knockout). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark and seal reach every page ONLY as merge binds through these image columns, not dropped in by hand. Built by hand so the text fields and all THREE image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (a converted PDF has no live merge fields and no data-merge image fields, so it would not bind — that was the killed spec's defect) and NOT a multi-up sheet: document_merge_data_layout emits one page per row, so the template holds exactly one section's worth of fields.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd/.idml carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it produces ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record per-section proof page is the correct, connector-doable shape. Supplied as an input, not a chain output. THREE image columns (@Hero distinct per row, @Wordmark and @Seal identical across all rows) mean the merge resolves three prepped assets per page — the section's own graded print hero plus the two shared brand marks — giving the chain-produced wordmark and seal a real, connector-doable path onto every page without any free-form placement (mirrors AO-74's @image/@Wordmark and AO-75's @Portrait/@TierBadge two-image-column patterns, extended to three).

inputs.name: marisol_section_roster.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: section,headline,subhead,@Hero,@Wordmark,@Seal and 6 rows, one per homepage section, in this order: (1) section 'Stays', headline 'Stays Above the Blue', subhead 'Twelve clifftop suites, each opening onto the sea.', @Hero 'stays_hero_print.jpg'; (2) section 'Weddings', headline 'Vows on the Cliff', subhead 'A private terrace above the Marisol blue.', @Hero 'weddings_hero_print.jpg'; (3) section 'Coastline', headline 'The Marisol Coastline', subhead 'Hidden coves and terraced villages along the shore.', @Hero 'coastline_hero_print.jpg'; (4) section 'Spa', headline 'The Sea-Cave Spa', subhead 'Thermal pools carved into the rock.', @Hero 'spa_hero_print.jpg'; (5) section 'Dining', headline 'Dining at Golden Hour', subhead 'Sea-to-table plates as the sun drops.', @Hero 'dining_hero_print.jpg'; (6) section 'Contact', headline 'Find the Cove', subhead 'Reservations open for the coming season.', @Hero 'contact_hero_print.jpg'. The @Wordmark column holds the SAME file 'marisol_wordmark.svg' in EVERY row, and the @Seal column holds the SAME file 'marisol_seal.png' in EVERY row, so the merge drops the two shared brand marks onto every section page as merge binds (never free-form placement). The @Hero column holds each section's DISTINCT full-bleed A4 PRINT hero (the ~3579 x 2551 px downscaled crop), NOT the web-sized banner. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<section>>,<<headline>>,<<subhead>> and the three @image-path columns @Hero,@Wordmark,@Seal.
inputs.realism_notes: Six rows => the merge must produce exactly six finished proof pages (page-count = row-count gate). @Hero carries a DISTINCT section PRINT-hero filename per row (stays_hero_print.jpg ... contact_hero_print.jpg — the full-bleed A4 print crops, which the agent must produce and upload under those exact names), while @Wordmark and @Seal carry the identical shared marks in all six rows — proving all three image columns land in the deliverable. The two print heroes from source A (Stays, Weddings), two from source B (Coastline, Spa) and two from source C (Dining, Contact) means the matched grade is visible down the whole page. Headlines/sub-heads bind verbatim; the agent does not rewrite copy. The web-sized banners are a separate live-site deliverable and are NOT merge inputs.

inputs.name: coastal_stock_source_A_warm_villa.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless stock capture of a whitewashed clifftop villa with terracotta roofs and white terrace parasols above a turquoise sea, ~4500-5000 px on the long edge (full-resolution stock still). Shot in WARM late-afternoon light with a distinct amber cast, slightly UNDEREXPOSED and flat in contrast as if straight off the camera. The whitewashed villa walls (the natural neutral reference) currently read too amber/warm; open sky fills the right third for headline space. Real render of stone, plaster, roof-tile and water texture, candid documentary travel-stock feel, no text, no watermark, wide 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: The stock library licenses at full camera resolution (~4500-5000 px), so ALL crops cut from it — a full-bleed A4 print hero (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI at trim) and a web banner for each of the Stays and Weddings sections — are DOWNSCALE-only, no upscaling anywhere. Its whitewashed walls read too amber and it is slightly underexposed, so the correct move toward the house target is a modest COOL-toward-warm-white plus an exposure LIFT. Feeds the Stays (print + wide web) and Weddings (print + tall web) section heroes. The whitewashed wall + white parasols are the in-frame natural neutral the grade is judged on, retained on the graded master.

inputs.name: coastal_stock_source_B_cool_bay.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless stock capture of a wider clifftop bay with whitewashed terraced houses, white sun parasols and moored boats on a turquoise sea, ~4500-5000 px on the long edge. Shot under COOL overcast / early blue-hour light with a distinct cool-blue cast, flat and slightly bright, and the horizon sits about 3 degrees off level (as a handheld stock frame often does). The whitewashed houses read cool/blue; open water fills the left third for headline space. Real texture of plaster, boat hulls and water, candid travel-stock feel, no text, no watermark, wide 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: Cool-blue cast + flat + ~3 deg tilt, so it needs its own correction: auto-straighten the horizon first, then a STRONG WARM shift toward the house warm-white with added contrast — the OPPOSITE direction from source A. Licensed at ~4500-5000 px so its full-bleed A4 print heroes (~3579 x 2551) and web banners all downscale. Feeds the Coastline (print + wide web) and Spa (print + tall web) section heroes. Whitewashed houses + parasols are its in-frame neutral reference.

inputs.name: coastal_stock_source_C_sunset_terrace.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: A REAL full-frame DSLR/mirrorless stock capture of a whitewashed clifftop dining terrace with white-clothed tables and parasols overlooking the sea, shot straight into a GOLDEN-HOUR sunset, ~4500-5000 px on the long edge. It is well-exposed and its whitewashed walls and white tablecloths ALREADY read as a warm sun-washed white that sits right on a warm-coastal house target — the warmth is the real golden-hour light, correctly captured, NOT a white-balance error. Warm sky fills the upper/right area for headline space. Real texture of plaster, linen and sea, candid travel-stock feel, no text, no watermark, wide 3:2 landscape.
inputs.realism_notes: THE UNDISCLOSED TRAP source. It looks like the frame that should be pushed hardest toward 'golden', but its whitewashed walls and white linens ALREADY sit on the warm-coastal target and it is correctly exposed. The correct move is to HOLD white balance (at most a tiny cool nudge) and only match exposure/black-point — warming it further to chase the sunset pushes its walls off the shared white point and breaks the set match. The brief states the goal (one house look) but does NOT disclose that this source is already on target; a naive agent that 'warms everything to golden hour' fails here. Feeds the Dining (print + wide web) and Contact (print + tall web) section heroes. Licensed at ~4500-5000 px so every crop — full-bleed A4 print hero and web banner alike — downscales.

inputs.name: marisol_wordmark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'MARISOL COVE' wordmark lockup printed on off-white textured paper: an elegant high-contrast cream/deep-teal serif wordmark with a small minimalist wave glyph above the text, deep-teal ink on a slightly warm off-white paper ground (NOT transparent, NOT pure white). The whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, ~2 deg rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw — forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten -> crisp -> crop-to-bounds -> knock the off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. Its counters trace filled-white on the off-white ground and read correctly on the template's CREAM masthead panel (light ground) — no dark-ground knockout is claimed. A text-to-image generator renders clean legible lettering. One of the two brand marks that CAN become clean vector line art.

inputs.name: marisol_seal_photo.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A close-up PHOTOGRAPH of a small embossed brass founder's seal / medallion reading 'MARISOL COVE - EST. MMXIX' around a wave relief, shot on a dark surface: shiny metallic brass with specular highlights, soft reflections, raised embossed relief and smooth tonal gradients across the metal. Clearly a photographed glossy metal object, not flat line art — full of sheen and gradient.
inputs.realism_notes: THE TRIAGE / TRAP mark. It looks like 'just the other logo', but it is a photographed metallic surface full of gradients and specular sheen: feeding it to image_vectorize returns a flat, muddy silhouette that destroys the brass. The correct treatment is crop-to-bounds -> image_remove_background to transparency -> keep as a high-resolution RASTER placed via @Seal. Getting it wrong is invisible in a thumbnail and only shows when the seal prints flat and dead on the proof. The second brand mark, the one that CANNOT survive a trace.

outputs.name: section_heroes_x6
outputs.spec: Two matched sets of six section heroes cut from the three match-graded masters, plus the three retained graded masters. (A) PRINT set — six full-bleed A4-landscape print heroes (stays_hero_print.jpg, weddings_hero_print.jpg, coastline_hero_print.jpg, spa_hero_print.jpg, dining_hero_print.jpg, contact_hero_print.jpg), each ~3579 x 2551 px (= 303 x 216 mm bleed edge at ~300 DPI, ~300 DPI effective at the 297 x 210 mm trim), each an honest DOWNSCALE from its ~4500-5000 px source (existing pixels only, no upscale, no canvas-extend) — these bind to @Hero and fill the proof page edge-to-edge WITHOUT enlargement. (B) WEB set — six web-ready banners for the live site: three WIDE cinematic bands (stays_hero.jpg, coastline_hero.jpg, dining_hero.jpg, ~2400x1000, 12:5) and three TALLER feature framings (weddings_hero.jpg, spa_hero.jpg, contact_hero.jpg, ~1600x1200, 4:3), each also an honest downscale/reframe of its source, each leaving clear open sky or water on one side for the headline. (C) the three RETAINED full-frame graded masters (coastal_source_A/B/C_graded, whitewashed-wall + parasol reference still in frame) the harness keeps as the match-grading artifacts. Acceptance (grader-checked, decoupled claims): (a) the match is graded on the THREE RETAINED graded masters — their whitewashed-wall / white-parasol reference regions read ONE common warm-coastal white point and their deep cliff/rock shadows floor at ONE common soft near-black (deep, not clipped to zero, no channel at 0), while each stays true to its scene; (b) framing/copy-space is checked separately on the delivered section crops; (c) every crop is a downscale from its declared ~4500-5000 px source — in particular each full-bleed print hero reaches ~300 DPI at the A4 trim WITHOUT any enlargement, and is a DISTINCT crop from the web-sized banner. Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint), exposure and black-point move applied to EACH of the three sources — the moves must be NON-IDENTICAL (source A cooled-to-warm-white and lifted, source B warmed strongly and straightened, source C held on white balance), proving the set was matched, not blanket-corrected.

outputs.name: MarisolCove_SectionProof_x6.pdf
outputs.spec: Exactly six press-ready A4-landscape (297 x 210 mm) homepage-section proof pages — ONE single-record page per roster section (page-count = row-count = 6) — exported in a SINGLE render call from the one-record-per-page data-merge with 3 mm bleed at ~300 DPI; each page binds its section/headline/subhead verbatim from the roster, places that section's match-graded PRINT-resolution hero full-bleed via @Hero (a downscale from the ~4500-5000 px source, ~300 DPI effective at the 297 x 210 mm trim — no web crop is enlarged to fill the page), the vectorized wordmark in the cream masthead panel via @Wordmark, and the transparent-ground embossed seal in the corner via @Seal. The Dining page simply sits among the six as one page of this proof book, not a separately exported file (document_render_layout exports the whole merged document, never one named record).

outputs.name: marisol_wordmark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the wordmark, traced only AFTER the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark and knocked to transparency — razor-sharp at masthead scale with no captured paper ground and no ~2 deg skew. Its counters read correctly on the template's light cream masthead panel.

outputs.name: marisol_seal.png
outputs.spec: The embossed brass founder's seal, cropped to bounds and knocked to a transparent ground via image_remove_background, kept as a HIGH-RESOLUTION RASTER (>=300 px square, so it prints >=300 DPI at ~25 mm) with all its metallic sheen and relief intact — deliberately NOT vectorized (a trace would flatten the brass to a muddy silhouette). Placed on every proof page via @Seal.

connector_workflow.note: Search the stock library for a high-resolution widescreen clifftop-villa coastal shot with whitewashed walls, terracotta roofs and open sky on one side. Returns low-res candidates; choose one large enough (~4500-5000 px) to cut a full-bleed A4 print hero AND a web banner for two section slots without upscaling.

License and download source A (warm late-afternoon villa) at full resolution (~4500-5000 px) — license BEFORE use. Large enough that the Stays and Weddings full-bleed A4 print heroes and their web banners all downscale from it.

Search the stock library for a wider clifftop-bay coastal shot (terraced houses, parasols, boats) with open water on one side — a DIFFERENTLY-lit frame of the same coastline so the campaign can vary section to section.
License and download source B (cool overcast bay) at full resolution — license before use. Feeds the Coastline and Spa print heroes and web banners.

Search the stock library for a whitewashed clifftop dining-terrace coastal shot in golden-hour light with open warm sky for headline space. Choose a large source (~4500-5000 px) for the Dining and Contact heroes.
License and download source C (golden-hour dining terrace) at full resolution — license before use. Feeds the Dining and Contact print heroes and web banners.

ESTABLISH the house warm-coastal look on source A and record it as the target the other two must hit. A is amber and underexposed, so COOL the white balance toward the house warm-white until the whitewashed villa walls read the target warm-white (kill the excess amber), LIFT exposure a touch for the airy premium feel, then set the black point so the deep cliff shade floors at the house soft near-black (deep, not clipped). Reason temp/tint/exposure/black to THIS frame's own walls and shadows; these reported numbers DEFINE the common target. Authored from primitives, NOT a preset, NOT auto_tone. Replaces the deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation. Report the move.

Source B's horizon is ~3 deg off level — straighten it FIRST so the later crops are cut against a true horizon and the sea line is flat. Only source B is tilted; A and C skip this (deciding which is part of the job).

Match source B to the target set on A — the OPPOSITE-direction correction. B is cool-blue and flat, so WARM the white balance STRONGLY until its whitewashed houses land on the SAME warm-white as A, add contrast to fix the flatness, and seat its cliff shadows on the SAME soft near-black. Its numbers must be clearly different from A's (a big warm shift, not A's cool shift) — copying A's settings would leave B cold and mismatched. Report the move.

THE TRAP FRAME. Source C is golden-hour but its whitewashed walls and white linens ALREADY read on the house warm-white and it is correctly exposed. The correct move is to HOLD white balance (at most a tiny cool nudge to sit exactly on target) and only match exposure and the black-point to A and B. A naive agent that 'warms everything to golden hour' (or copies B's big warm shift) will drive C's walls off-neutral orange and break the set match. Decision driven by THIS frame's walls, not the batch. Report that white balance was essentially HELD and only tone matched.

Cut the Stays PRINT hero: a FULL-BLEED A4-landscape crop (~3579 x 2551 px = 303 x 216 mm bleed edge at ~300 DPI, ~300 DPI effective at the 297 x 210 mm trim) from graded source A, framing the villa RIGHT so open sky on the left stays clear for the headline. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only from the ~4500-5000 px master — never generative-expand, never enlarge. Binds to @Hero and fills the Stays proof page edge-to-edge as a downscale. The retained coastal_source_A_graded (walls in frame) is the match-grading artifact; the match is graded THERE, not on this crop.

Cut the Weddings PRINT hero: a second FULL-BLEED A4-landscape crop (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI at trim) from the SAME graded source A — a different region/framing of the same shot so Stays and Weddings share one image identity — open sky kept on one side for the headline. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only. Binds to @Hero for the Weddings proof page.

Cut the Coastline PRINT hero: a FULL-BLEED A4-landscape crop (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI at trim) from the straightened, match-graded source B, framing the terraced houses to one side with open water clear for the headline. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only from the ~4500-5000 px master. Binds to @Hero for the Coastline proof page.

Cut the Spa PRINT hero: a second FULL-BLEED A4-landscape crop (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI at trim) from the SAME graded source B, a calmer water-and-rock region, copy space kept. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only. Binds to @Hero for the Spa proof page.

Cut the Dining PRINT hero: a FULL-BLEED A4-landscape crop (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI at trim) from graded source C, framing the terrace tables to one side with the warm sky clear for the headline. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only from the ~4500-5000 px master. Binds to @Hero for the Dining proof page.

Cut the Contact PRINT hero: a second FULL-BLEED A4-landscape crop (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI at trim) from the SAME graded source C, an open sea-and-sky region, copy space kept. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only. Binds to @Hero for the Contact proof page. The six PRINT heroes now share ONE house warm-coastal look, two cut from each of the three match-graded masters, each a downscale that fills the full-bleed proof frame without upscaling.

Cut the Stays WEB banner: a WIDE cinematic band (~2400x1000, 12:5) from graded source A, villa framed RIGHT so open sky on the left stays clear for the headline. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only from the ~4500-5000 px master. This is the live-site banner (a DISTINCT crop from the print hero), never generative-expand.

Cut the Weddings WEB banner: a TALLER feature framing (~1600x1200, 4:3) from the SAME graded source A, open sky kept on one side for the headline. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only. Live-site banner.

Cut the Coastline WEB banner: a WIDE band (~2400x1000) from graded source B, terraced houses to one side with open water clear for the headline. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only. Live-site banner.
Cut the Spa WEB banner: a TALLER frame (~1600x1200) from the SAME graded source B, a calmer water-and-rock region, copy space kept. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only. Live-site banner.

Cut the Dining WEB banner: a WIDE band (~2400x1000) from graded source C, terrace tables to one side with warm sky clear for the headline. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only. Live-site banner.

Cut the Contact WEB banner: a TALLER frame (~1600x1200) from the SAME graded source C, an open sea-and-sky region, copy space kept. onSubjectClipping='extract', DOWNSCALE-only. Live-site banner. The six web banners are the live-site deliverable; the six print heroes feed the proof book.
Prep-before-trace step 1: the wordmark scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed — straighten it so the vector edges come out square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward clean white so the deep-teal lettering separates hard from the ground — a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the wordmark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). On the off-white ground the enclosed counters trace filled-white and read correctly on the template's light cream masthead panel — no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, transparent) into a clean SVG for the section mastheads. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette — the trap this prep chain avoids. The flat wordmark is the mark that CAN become clean vector.

Triage DIVERGES here: the founder's seal is a PHOTOGRAPH of an embossed brass medallion — full of sheen, reflections and relief gradients — so it CANNOT become clean line art (vectorizing it would return a flat muddy silhouette and kill the brass). Crop only to the tight bounds of the medallion; do NOT send it to image_vectorize.

Knock the dark surround to transparency so only the brass seal remains, keeping every specular highlight and relief gradient intact. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill, NOT a solid fill). This preserves the metallic sheen the vector path would have destroyed.

Square-crop/resize the transparent brass seal to a 1:1 corner mark at >=300 px square so it prints >=300 DPI at ~25 mm. Kept as a HIGH-RESOLUTION RASTER placed via @Seal on every page. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only — never enlarged past the photographed source.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining throughout. Three stock tributaries fan in from the stock library: search(1)->license(2)=source A, search(3)->license(4)=source B, search(5)->license(6)=source C. Each source runs its OWN adaptive match-grade: A grades directly (7, the REFERENCE look — cool-to-warm-white + lift, its reported numbers DEFINE the target); B straightens first (8) then grades (9, the OPPOSITE correction — strong warm + contrast to the SAME white point); C grades (10, the TRAP — white balance HELD, only tone matched). Each match-graded master then forks into FOUR crops consuming only that master — a full-bleed A4 PRINT hero and a web banner for each of its two sections, all DOWNSCALE-only from the ~4500-5000 px master: A -> stays_hero_print(11) + weddings_hero_print(12) + stays_hero web(17) + weddings_hero web(18); B -> coastline_hero_print(13) + spa_hero_print(14) + coastline_hero web(19) + spa_hero web(20); C -> dining_hero_print(15) + contact_hero_print(16) + dining_hero web(21) + contact_hero web(22). The six PRINT heroes (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI at trim) bind to @Hero and fill the proof page full-bleed as a downscale — never a web crop enlarged; the six web banners (2400x1000 wide / 1600x1200 tall) are the separate live-site deliverable. The wordmark runs a genuine prep-before-trace chain: straighten(23)->crisp(24)->crop_to_bounds(25)->remove_background to transparency(26)->vectorize(27)=marisol_wordmark.svg. The seal TRIAGES the other way: crop_to_bounds(28)->remove_background to transparency(29)->crop_and_resize(30)=marisol_seal.png, deliberately never touching image_vectorize. The six PRINT heroes plus the two prepped marks converge into the upload session(31)->finalize(32)->document_merge_data_layout(33), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the roster CSV and emits one merged page per row, resolving @Hero (that section's print hero), @Wordmark and @Seal (shared) per row. The merged set is exported ONCE by document_render_layout(34) to the single A4-landscape proof book (six pages, one section per page). Only the three searches and the four supplied inputs (template, roster CSV, wordmark scan, seal photo) originate outside the chain; nothing is upscaled or generatively expanded.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship with difficulty from DEPTH, not plumbing: 34 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (asset_* stock+storage, image_* grade/straighten/crop/vectorize/knockout, document_* merge/export), above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the 2 upload steps and the 2 auto_straighten auto-ops — the 30 remaining substantive steps carry the difficulty. The core is not a repeated recipe: the three sources take THREE different reasoned corrections in three different directions (A cooled-to-warm-white and lifted; B warmed strongly and straightened; C held on white balance and only tone-matched) all forced to converge on a SINGLE house target read off each frame's own whitewashed-wall and cliff-shadow references — a blanket batch correction cannot pass. Layered on top: twelve section heroes cut four-per-master (a full-bleed A4 PRINT hero at ~300 DPI-at-trim plus a web banner for each section), all honest DOWNSCALES from camera-scale stock with distinct copy space — so the full-bleed proof hero fills the page WITHOUT any upscaling (the defect a skeptic caught: a web-sized 2400/1600 px crop bound full-bleed to an ~3579 px A4 frame would have been an enlargement); a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white wordmark scan; a two-way TRIAGE of the two brand marks (flat wordmark vectorized to clean line art vs photographed embossed seal kept as transparent raster because a trace would flatten its brass); and a three-image-column one-record-per-page data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template producing a single six-page proof book. Respects every hard limit: no generative fill/expand, no text-to-image, no upscaling (stock licensed large then cropped DOWN for BOTH print and web heroes), no inpainting, no from-scratch layout; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT used (the template is a supplied authored .indd/.idml) — removing the killed spec's merge-target defect; document_render_layout makes ONE whole-document export, not three per-artboard exports (the killed spec's second defect); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract'; image_fill_area and image_apply_color_overlay are unused; deprecated image_adjust_color_temperature / _vibrance_and_saturation / _highlights / _brightness_and_contrast are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): the three licensed sources start under different light and must converge on ONE house warm-coastal look, judged on each frame's own in-frame natural neutral (the whitewashed villa walls / white parasols) landing on one common warm-white and the cliff shade on one common soft near-black; the agent works BY EYE and REPORTS the per-source white-balance/exposure/black it applied, and those moves must be NON-IDENTICAL (A cooled, B warmed, C held) — a set each 'auto-fixed' to look fine alone diverges at the walls and is rejected, and identical reported numbers across the three are a visible fail. The merge adds a second checkable gate (page-count must equal roster row-count = 6, since document_merge_data_layout is one-record-per-page). HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS: (1) cross-asset match-grade of three differently-lit sources to a common warm-white and soft-black, each needing its own opposite-direction correction reasoned to its own walls; (2) a two-way triage of the two brand marks needing DIFFERENT correct treatments — the flat wordmark prepped-and-vectorized to clean line art, the photographed embossed brass seal knocked to transparency and kept as high-res raster because a trace would flatten its sheen (a mistake invisible until the proof prints dead); (3) prep-before-trace discipline on the skewed, off-white, margin-padded wordmark scan (straighten->crisp->crop-to-bounds->knock-to-transparency) before vectorize; (4) the resolution split — each section's full-bleed A4 @Hero must be a DISTINCT print-resolution crop (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI at trim) cut DOWN from the ~4500-5000 px source, never the web-sized 2400/1600 px banner enlarged to fill the page. TRAP the BRIEF does not disclose: source C is a golden-hour frame whose whitewashed walls and white linens ALREADY sit on the house warm-white and is correctly exposed, so the correct move is to HOLD white balance and only match tone; the brief says only to bring all three to one warm-coastal look and warns generally to 'judge the sunset frame on its own walls' but never states that C is already on target — a naive agent that warms all three to golden hour (or copies source B's big warm shift) pushes C's walls off-neutral and breaks the set match. A second undisclosed pitfall: the wordmark can be vectorized but the seal cannot survive it, and only the supplied single-record authored .indd/.idml merges (a convert_pdf_to_indd or multi-up template will not bind). A third: binding a web-sized hero into the full-bleed A4 frame would silently upscale it — the agent must cut a separate print-resolution hero. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (decoupled so no artifact is graded on a region it crops away): (a) the common warm-white and soft-black are graded on the THREE RETAINED full-frame graded masters (whitewashed-wall + parasol reference still in frame), never on a reframed section crop; (b) framing/copy-space is checked separately on the delivered section crops; (c) every hero crop is a genuine DOWNSCALE from its declared ~4500-5000 px source, and each section's full-bleed A4 @Hero is a print-resolution crop (~3579 x 2551 px, ~300 DPI effective at the 297 x 210 mm trim) never a web-sized banner enlarged — no upscaling anywhere in the merge; plus the agent reports the three non-identical per-source WB/exposure/black moves; the wordmark is a clean skew-free transparent-ground vector; the seal is a transparent-ground raster >=300 px square with sheen intact (NOT vectorized); and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI A4-landscape proof page per roster section.
